stem: A 27-year-old woman has a firm, nontender nodule along her cesarean scar 2 months after delivery. It is excised. Under routine staining the specimen shows multinucleated giant cells and fibroblasts, with chronic inflammatory cells. The slide is then viewed under polarized light (see the picture).
oneliner: 27F + firm nodule at cesarean scar 2 months later + giant cells and fibroblasts on H&E + polarized light → what shows?
ask: What does polarized light microscopy of the nodule show?

options.C: Birefringent foreign fragments within giant cells

whyNot.A: Amyloid, seen only after **Congo red** staining, as extracellular deposits rather than a giant-cell nodule at a **surgical scar**
whyNot.B: Urate crystals of **gout**; a nodule at a **2-month-old cesarean scar** is not a tophus
whyNot.D: Calcium pyrophosphate of **pseudogout**, found in joint cartilage, not a **surgical scar**
whyNot.E: Giant cells at a **fresh surgical scar** form around material they cannot digest, usually suture, which polarizes

answer: Birefringent foreign material (e.g., suture) within multinucleated giant cells
why: A **foreign body granuloma** forms around material macrophages cannot digest, such as **suture, talc or silica**. Macrophages fuse into **multinucleated giant cells**, with fibroblasts. **Polarized light** makes the retained material **birefringent**, confirming the cause.

idea.rule: A giant-cell reaction around birefringent material at a surgical site = foreign body granuloma.
also: Suture, talc, silica and silicone can all cause it
Gout: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent urate crystals
Pseudogout: rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent crystals
Amyloid with Congo red: apple-green birefringence

stem: A 52-year-old woman has had trouble climbing stairs and combing her hair for 3 months. Her upper eyelids are violet and swollen, and creatine kinase is raised. Her upper back, shoulders and fingertips are then examined (see the picture).
oneliner: 52F + trouble climbing stairs, combing hair + violet swollen eyelids + high CK → what is seen on her back, shoulders and nailfolds?
ask: Which finding on her upper back, shoulders and nailfolds is most likely?

options.A: Tight shiny finger skin with lost creases
options.B: Silvery scaly plaques over the back
options.C: Net-like violet mottling of the shoulders
options.D: Violet upper-back erythema with dilated nailfold capillaries
options.E: Scarring discoid plaques with follicular plugs

whyNot.A: **Sclerodactyly** of systemic sclerosis; it does not explain **proximal weakness with a high CK**
whyNot.B: **Psoriasis** plaques; they do not come with **violet eyelids** and muscle weakness
whyNot.C: **Livedo reticularis** of vasculitis or antiphospholipid syndrome, not a muscle disease with **high CK**
whyNot.E: **Discoid lupus** lesions; her picture is **proximal weakness, violet eyelids and high CK**

answer: Shawl sign (and periungual capillary changes) of dermatomyositis
why: **Proximal weakness, violet eyelids (heliotrope) and high CK** point to **dermatomyositis**. Other skin signs are **Gottron papules**, the **shawl sign** (erythema across the upper back and shoulders) and **dilated periungual capillaries**. Adults carry a raised risk of an **underlying malignancy**.

idea.rule: Dermatomyositis skin signs: heliotrope eyelids, Gottron papules, shawl sign, nailfold changes.
also: Anti-Jo-1 (antisynthetase) with interstitial lung disease and mechanic's hands
Screen adults for ovarian, lung and GI cancer
